The B*_Q6 synonymous-codon residual association with yeast protein abundance is real (held-out 5-fold R^2 ~0.19 vs permutation null ~0) and partially reducible: a <=3-readout measured dictionary {measured_te, mrna_stability, turnover} captures ~24.5% of the Z-residualized abundance residual, surviving a selection-aware permutation null (null95 ~0.029, ~5x the naive fixed-subset null ~0.006); ~75% remains unexplained, and local codon-pair Q^(2) context adds no held-out signal. Certifies the residual as a real, partially-mediated (not irreducible) primitive over the tested readout family.

claims.statement: Hypothesis (tested, falsified): the B*_Q6 synonymous-codon residual on yeast protein abundance is an irreducible primitive -- a real held-out signal that NEITHER single-codon readout-dictionary compression NOR local codon-pair Q^(2) context captures. Result: source is real, but the {measured_te, mrna_stability, turnover} dictionary captures ~24.5% (selection-aware significant), so the residual is partially reducible, not irreducible. Explicit negative complementing the partial_mediation certificate.

A per-gene tRNA-supply readout (dos Reis tAI from yeast GtRNAdb tRNA gene-copy numbers + wobble) adds incremental held-out predictive power for Z-residualized yeast protein abundance BEYOND the measured {measured_te, mrna_stability, turnover} dictionary: 5-fold held-out delta-R^2 ~0.061 (base R^2 ~0.458 -> full ~0.519), exceeding a fixed-readout permutation null95 ~0.0007. Codon-level tRNA adaptation carries abundance information not captured by bulk measured translation efficiency, partly addressing the residual left unexplained by the partial_mediation dictionary.

Per-coordinate decomposition of the B*_Q6 -> yeast protein-abundance residual: of the 9 synonymous coordinates, 8 are real held-out abundance sources (K_AAA, Arg_AGR, Ile_AUA, Leu_CUN_vs_UUR, Leu_UUA_vs_UUG, Ser_UCR_vs_AGY, Thr_ACR_vs_ACY, f3_stress) and 1 (Ser_UCA_vs_UCG) is not; f3_stress carries the most residual energy (~20% of target, R^2~0.19) followed by Ile_AUA and Thr_ACR_vs_ACY. The measured {te,mrna_stability,turnover} dictionary's projection coverage exceeds the per-coordinate permutation null for the 8 real sources, but a large absolute residual energy remains unexplained per coordinate (e.g. f3_stress ~81% unexplained). Descriptive decomposition, not causal mediation.

The dominant B*_Q6 coordinate f3_stress (a global synonymous first-vs-last-codon direction across all 21 families) carrying ~20% of the abundance-residual energy is only MARGINALLY reachable by independent molecular measurements: the full {te,stability,turnover,localization,ptm,complex,tm,domain,mrna_abundance} readout set reaches best coverage 0.226 vs base {te,stability,turnover} 0.190 (increment +0.036, selection-aware-significant vs null95 0.027), but ~77.4% of f3_stress remains unexplained by ALL available measurements. The dominant frontier is largely orthogonal to current molecular readouts and needs new data/mechanism.

The dominant B*_Q6 coordinate f3_stress's protein-abundance contribution (P_f3, ~20% of target, ~77% orthogonal to static measured readouts) is PARTLY MEDIATED BY RIBOSOME DWELL: per-gene local ribosome occupancy features add held-out delta-R^2 ~0.019 over the {te,mrna_stability,turnover} dictionary (vs fixed-readout permutation null95 ~0.0013), and f3_stress couples positively to dwell (corr 0.162, p~8e-9, reproducing wobble-dwell). Since base already contains measured_te (footprint/mRNA), this is an increment beyond bulk TE -- a dynamic elongation mechanism partly explains f3_stress's abundance effect that static molecular readouts miss.

f3_stress's ribosome-dwell mediation of its protein-abundance contribution (P_f3) is LOCALIZED TO THE 5' TRANSLATIONAL RAMP, not the gene body: 5'-window dwell adds held-out delta-R^2 ~0.023 over {te,stability,turnover} (vs null95 ~0.0016, f3<->5'-dwell corr 0.156 p~3e-8), while 3'/body-window dwell is null (delta-R^2 ~-0.0002), and the joint 5'+3' increment ~= 5'-alone. Supports the translational-ramp hypothesis: the dominant frontier coordinate acts through slow-codon dwell at the 5' ribosome-loading region, increment beyond bulk measured_te.

Biological identity of f3_stress (the dominant B*_Q6 abundance coordinate): decomposing it into 21 synonymous family subcoordinates (exact, sum-consistency l2err~8e-16), 19/21 families are real held-out abundance sources, and the effect is DOMINATED BY GLYCINE (GGN) and ISOLEUCINE (AUU/AUC/AUA) synonymous choices (held-out R^2 0.079/0.063, energy 0.65/0.52), then Arginine (CGN, AGR), Gln, Phe, Thr, Val. So f3_stress is largely a Gly/Ile synonymous-choice axis (Ile-AUA is a known slow/wobble codon), not a uniform 'first-vs-last' artifact.

Cross-organism f3_stress->protein-abundance: the association DIRECTION generalizes near-universally (15/15 organisms held-out-significant vs permutation null after cds-length/total-codon/GC3/20-aa-composition controls, 14/15 POSITIVE; only the archaeon S. solfataricus negative), BUT the effect MAGNITUDE is strongly yeast-dominant. Held-out R^2: yeast 0.168 (clear outlier), lower-eukaryotes/some bacteria 0.01-0.05 (dicty, C.elegans, drosophila, pseudomonas, danio, bacillus), and MAMMALS negligible (human 0.0004, mouse 0.0006, rat 0.0008) -- the latter clear null only via large-n significance (explain <0.1% of variance). So the strong synonymous-codon->abundance coupling is a yeast (+lower-eukaryote/bacterial) phenomenon; in mammals the f3_stress axis is biologically negligible. NOTE: the experiment's pass gate is significance (held_out>null95), which overstates generality at large n; the honest reading is direction-universal, magnitude-yeast-dominant.

Why f3_stress is yeast-dominant: across 15 organisms its effect size = translational-selection strength x directional alignment. (1) Total synonymous-codon selection on abundance (independent 41-col full design) predicts f3 strength (Spearman rho=0.71). (2) f3_alignment sign predicts f3 direction 15/15, incl. the lone negative organism S. solfataricus (anti-aligned). Yeast is strongest because it has BY FAR the highest translational selection (syn_sel R^2=0.39, ~2x runner-up) AND positive f3 alignment (0.24). Counterexample E.coli: high selection (0.22) but f3 near-orthogonal (align 0.046) -> weak f3 (0.006), so alignment matters independently. Mammals: weak selection (0.05-0.08) -> negligible f3. So f3_stress is a 1-D proxy for the organism's codon-level translational selection; it is strong in yeast because yeast's translational selection is strongest. Caveat: n=15, no phylogenetic correction; alignment uses same-organism abundance preferences (direction-agreement partly definitional; non-circular core is the independent selection<->strength rho=0.71).

Cross-organism structure of the abundance-optimal synonymous-codon direction (15 organisms, 41-col synonymous contrast design). conservation_call=CLUSTERED: mean pairwise cosine 0.26 (not conserved>=0.6, not idiosyncratic), organized mainly by GENOMIC GC3 (GC3-delta vs cosine Pearson -0.36) more than by domain (same-domain 0.29 vs cross-domain 0.25). A weak UNIVERSAL CORE direction exists (mean held-out R^2 0.088; max yeast 0.30, E.coli 0.20). Yeast optimizes HARDEST (self-direction R^2 0.40) but in a relatively IDIOSYNCRATIC direction (core alignment 0.38, among the lowest); E.coli is core-aligned (0.77). f3_stress is a crude fixed proxy weakly aligned with everything (f3 vs core 0.26, vs yeast 0.20, vs E.coli 0.22). Caveat: n=15, no phylogenetic correction, optimal direction inferred from abundance-associated contrasts (not causal).

Window6 boundary set R biological-signature test (bridge BC1 empirical contact). The 10 R sense-codons (math/geometry-derived boundary, NO usage fitting) are systematically AVOIDED (lower abundance-preference than non-R sense codons) in ALL 15/15 organisms (cross-organism sign test ~ p 6e-5), but only 6/15 reach individual per-organism permutation significance, so the experiment's strict gate (>=8 significant) emits FAILED. Honest reading: the abstract Window6 boundary R HAS a real, directionally-universal biological signature (it is the set of avoided codons), under-detected by the per-organism gate (small-genome power). Same pattern as f3 cross-organism (direction universal, per-organism magnitude varies). Supports BC1's empirical prong; the math forcing prong still pending. Follow-on: a cross-organism sign-test gate would call this supported.

Mechanism for why Window6 boundary set R is biologically avoided (Route L): the 10 R sense-codons are systematically tRNA-POOR (lower dos-Reis tAI weight, from GtRNAdb tGCN+wobble) than non-R sense codons in 31/40 organisms (cross-organism sign test binomial two-sided p~7e-4; 9/40 opposite, so predominant not universal). So the math-defined Window6 boundary R = the translationally non-optimal / tRNA-scarce codons -> they are decoded slowly and selected against -> avoided (Route L). Gives the abstract boundary a real mechanistic biological identity. Deterministic; tAI from GtRNAdb. Caveat: tAI is a supply proxy, not direct decoding-rate; 40 organisms no phylogenetic correction.

Route N: the cross-organism universal optimal synonymous-codon direction (the weak universal core of Route K) is substantially the tRNA-adaptation direction. Across 11 organisms with both proteomes and GtRNAdb tRNA-gene copies, each organism's abundance-optimal direction (full 41-dim synonymous contrast) aligns with its dos-Reis tAI tRNA-supply direction at mean cos 0.267 (median 0.302; cross-organism sign test 10/11 positive, p~5.9e-3; normal-approx p~7e-7), and the tRNA direction ALONE recovers ~43% (pooled held-out R2 ratio 0.434; median per-organism 0.30) of the abundance signal the full optimal direction captures (mean tRNA-alone held-out R2=0.059 vs self R2=0.136). The tRNA direction also aligns with the cross-organism universal core at cos 0.246 (9/11 positive, p~0.033). So translational selection toward tRNA-abundant codons is a MAJOR but PARTIAL (~43%) component of universal codon optimality, not the whole thing -- consistent with f3 residual dominance and the ~24.5% reducibility of B*_Q6. Deterministic; tAI from GtRNAdb tGCN+wobble. Caveat: 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb), tAI is a supply proxy not a direct decoding rate, no phylogenetic correction.

Route O: the NON-tRNA component of universal codon optimality is the f3-stress translational-selection axis, NOT GC mutational bias. After Gram-Schmidt-removing each organism's tRNA-adaptation direction from its 41-dim abundance-optimal synonymous direction (Route N), the residual aligns with the f3-stress axis (mean cos 0.139, 10/11 organisms positive, cross-organism sign-test p~5.9e-3, normal-approx p~6e-6) and is ANTI-aligned with the GC3 mutational-bias axis (mean cos -0.073, 10/11 negative). The GC3 and f3-stress reference directions are nearly anti-parallel in this contrast space (cos -0.905), so the residual selects the f3/translational-selection pole over the GC/mutation pole (paired |cos_f3|>|cos_gc| in 11/11 organisms, p~4.9e-4). Combined with Route N (~43% tRNA-adaptation), B*_Q6 codon optimality decomposes into TWO translational-selection mechanisms -- tRNA-supply adaptation + f3-ramp stress -- with GC mutational bias as the opposite pole, not a positive driver. Deterministic; 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb). Caveat: f3 cosine magnitude is modest (0.139) though directionally consistent; GC/f3 near-antiparallel means the two readouts are not independent; observational not causal; E.coli/P.aeruginosa/etc lack GtRNAdb (needs_data); no phylogenetic correction.

Route P: universal codon optimality is NOT 2-dimensional (tRNA + f3) -- a universal THIRD selection axis exists. Projecting each organism's 41-dim abundance-optimal synonymous direction onto span{d_tRNA, d_f3} captures only mean 13.0% of its norm^2 (captured_fraction mean 0.130, median 0.102, 11/11 organisms < 0.5); the residual-after-both direction d_perp retains ~93% of the optimal norm. d_perp is NOT noise: systematically positive held-out R2 (mean 0.066, 11/11 positive, p~4.9e-4) recovering ~64% of the self-direction abundance R2 (d_perp/self ratio mean 0.640), and CROSS-ORGANISM ALIGNED (55-pair mean cosine 0.179, 38/55 positive, sign-test p~3.2e-3, normal-approx p~1.6e-6). In 8/11 organisms d_perp alone out-predicts the tRNA+f3 plane combined (two-axis recovers ~40% of self R2). So codon optimality has at least THREE universal selection dimensions; tRNA-supply adaptation (Route N) + f3-stress (Route O) are real but together a MINORITY of the optimal direction's geometry and predictive content. The identity of the third universal axis d_perp is the open frontier. Deterministic; 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb). Caveat: cosines modest; observational not causal; no phylogenetic correction; d_perp is an orthogonal-complement residual so its mechanistic identity needs separate characterization.

Route Q: the third universal codon-optimality axis d_perp (Route P) is provisionally identified as the within-synonymous-family USAGE-FREQUENCY axis (preferred-codon bias). Across 11 organisms d_perp aligns with the within-family usage-frequency direction at mean cos 0.128 (11/11 organisms positive, cross-organism sign-test p~4.9e-4) -- the ONLY tested candidate axis clearing the cross-organism gate. Other candidates are weak/non-significant: position composition (pos3_C 0.084 7/11 ns, pos1_C 0.079 8/11 ns), residual GC3 (0.054 9/11 p~0.03 marginal), the other 8 B*_Q6 synonymous coordinates, amino-acid/position composites -- none explain d_perp. So codon optimality has THREE universal selection axes: tRNA-supply adaptation (Route N), f3-stress 5'-ramp translational selection (Route O), and the genome-wide preferred-codon usage-frequency bias (Route Q), the last distinct from tRNA-supply. Deterministic; 11 organisms (proteome intersect GtRNAdb). Caveat: cosine modest (0.128); usage-frequency correlates with expression so part of this reflects the abundance-optimal direction recovering the preferred-codon set, and the deeper driver of usage-frequency beyond tRNA is itself composite/open; observational; no phylogenetic correction. Also exports per-codon d_perp + tRNA-supply vectors in the codon-Q6 6-bit frame (codon_q6_selection_vectors.json) fulfilling the Window6-codon bridge BC5 data request.

Route R: the third universal codon-optimality axis d_perp (Route P/Q, the within-family preferred-codon/usage-frequency direction) is a GENUINE cross-organism SELECTION signal -- NOT a GC/mutational projection and NOT the wobble-decoding axis. GC-null defeat: after orthogonalizing d_perp against the GC3 direction it remains cross-organism aligned (55-pair mean cosine 0.177, 38/55 positive, sign-test p~3.2e-3) and still predicts protein abundance held-out (mean R2 0.071, 11/11 positive, p~5e-4) -- essentially unchanged from pre-orthogonalization (0.179/0.066); GC3 alone gives only R2 0.028. So d_perp is not mutational GC bias. Wobble test: d_perp per-codon loadings do NOT cluster by wobble-decoding class (exact-match vs wobble, NNU/NNC vs NNA/NNG, 2-codon U/C splits) -- not the tRNA-modification/wobble axis. The leading remaining identity -- CSC / mRNA-stability codon optimality (codon-mediated decay) and 5'-vs-CDS-body positional localization -- requires external data (published CSC vectors / mRNA half-lives / positional CDS) and is flagged needs_external (repo holds only whole-CDS codon counts). Deterministic; 11 organisms. Net: the third optimality axis is a real preferred-codon SELECTION pressure distinct from tRNA-supply, the 5'-ramp f3 axis, GC mutation, and wobble decoding; most plausibly mRNA-stability-driven, pending external CSC/half-life data. Oracle (chatgpt-pro) independently ranked CSC/mRNA-stability as the #1 candidate.
